approachQuestion.prompt:
Crossing support beams

Given two closed integer-coordinate segments AB and CD, return whether their intersection is nonempty. Touching endpoints, collinear overlap and zero-length segments count as intersections.

Example 1: A=(0,0),B=(4,4),C=(0,4),D=(4,0) -> true.
Example 2: A=(0,0),B=(4,0),C=(2,0),D=(6,0) -> true.
Example 3: A=B=(1,1),C=(0,0),D=(2,2) -> true.
Example 4: A=(0,0),B=(1,0),C=(2,0),D=(3,0) -> false.

Constraints and assumptions: Coordinates are integers in [-10^6,10^6]. Use exact signed 64-bit arithmetic; return one boolean. Boundary contact must be classified exactly. Choose the best time bound among the offered correct methods, then the least auxiliary storage when time ties.

options.text: Compute orientations of C,D about AB and A,B about CD. Accept a zero orientation with the endpoint in the other segment's closed box. Otherwise require strictly opposite signs in both orientation pairs, comparing signs directly.
options.feedback: An endpoint-on-segment test handles all touching, overlap and degenerate cases; strict opposite sides then characterize a proper crossing. Direct sign comparisons avoid overflow from multiplying cross values.

options.text: Return true only when both orientation pairs have strictly opposite signs.
options.feedback: This rejects collinear overlapping segments such as AB=(0,0)-(4,0), CD=(2,0)-(6,0), whose intersection is nonempty.

options.text: Return true whenever the two inclusive bounding rectangles overlap.
options.feedback: AB=(0,0)-(2,2), CD=(0,2)-(0,1) have overlapping boxes but no common segment point.

options.text: Return true whenever the supporting infinite lines intersect, and false for parallel lines.
options.feedback: AB=(0,0)-(1,0), CD=(2,-1)-(2,1) have intersecting lines at (2,0), outside AB. It also rejects collinear overlaps.

feedback.reason: Distinguish a proper crossing from touching and collinear overlap without unsafe sign products.
details: Compute the four orientation cross products. First accept any zero orientation whose tested endpoint is inside the other segment's inclusive bounding box. Otherwise accept only if the two orientations about each segment have strictly opposite signs, comparing signs without multiplying cross values.

Opposite orientation signs detect a proper crossing, while zero orientations need explicit on-segment tests for touching or collinear overlap. Compare signs directly; multiplying cross products can overflow despite each individual product fitting.

Otherwise require strictly opposite signs in both orientation pairs, comparing signs directly.”: An endpoint-on-segment test handles all touching, overlap and degenerate cases; strict opposite sides then characterize a proper crossing. Direct sign comparisons avoid overflow from multiplying cross values.
“Return true only when both orientation pairs have strictly opposite signs.”: This rejects collinear overlapping segments such as AB=(0,0)-(4,0), CD=(2,0)-(6,0), whose intersection is nonempty.
“Return true whenever the two inclusive bounding rectangles overlap.”: AB=(0,0)-(2,2), CD=(0,2)-(0,1) have overlapping boxes but no common segment point.

“Return true whenever the supporting infinite lines intersect, and false for parallel lines.”: AB=(0,0)-(1,0), CD=(2,-1)-(2,1) have intersecting lines at (2,0), outside AB. It also rejects collinear overlaps.

complexityQuestion.prompt: Analyze only the revealed method (orientation-with-boundaries). Let C denote the maximum coordinate magnitude, with coordinates represented as fixed-width words. Choose its tightest standard worst-case time and auxiliary-space pair.
constraints: Exact signed 64-bit integer arithmetic, casting before calculations; arithmetic and comparisons cost one unit. No arbitrary-precision operations.
Iterative method, no recursion or hashing, no input copies. Auxiliary space includes all temporary state and buffers, excluding supplied input and returned output.
Include initialization and any copying; no hidden preprocessing or cache.

feedback.reason: Four orientations and fixed endpoint checks do not enumerate coordinates.
details: Exactly four orientations and constant many endpoint-box and sign tests are performed. Each cross product has magnitude at most 8*10^12, safely representable; multiplying two such cross values would not be safe and is not performed. All retained vectors and products are constant-size.
